Category: Object.
Subject: piano accordion.
Style: Italian mother-of-pearl.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a module for a static piano accordion model styled with Italian mother-of-pearl, sized around 0.45m, built from parts with appropriate geometry, colors, and textures rather than joints since it's a static object.

Now I'm working out the layout: treble case with the keyboard on one side, bass case with buttons on the other, bellows connecting them along the X axis, standing roughly 0.40m tall and 0.20m deep, with keys protruding forward and stacked along the vertical axis.

So keys sit on the +Z face with length along X and stacking along Y—white keys sized small protruding boxes, black keys shorter and placed toward the inner edge. I'm also thinking about adding decorative grille panels, pearl inlay swirls, and register switch buttons to the treble case for visual detail.

For the bass case, I'm planning a grid of cylindrical pearl buttons (6x8) merged on the +Z face plus a strap bar. For the bellows, I'm working out how to build the accordion-fold geometry—looking at zigzag profiles or stacked frustum-like boxes to represent each pleat realistically.

Now I'm settling on an approach: 16 alternating segments of varying size and depth to create a ridged bellows look, styled as pearly iridescent celluloid plates with gold trim and dark red bellows, plus thin pearl-strip wedges along the pleat edges for an authentic Italian accordion finish.

I'm defining a custom pearl paint function that mixes noise-based color swirls across off-white, pink, teal, and lilac tones, along with the structural parts: a pearl-painted treble case body framed in gold with contrasting lacquer accents.

Now I'm working out the keyboard geometry — placing merged white and black key meshes with correct spacing and skip patterns to mimic a real accordion keyboard, positioning them along the case front near the bellows side.

For the opposite side of the case, I'm planning a decorative pearl panel with a gold decal, maybe a floral swirl motif and a brand-style scroll text, as a separate textured plane on the case's front face.

Now moving to the treble side's top grille—a perforated gold-on-dark panel oriented upward, plus small pearl register switch cylinders, and an end cap on the +X face with a pearl swirl and gold floral emblem. Then I'm laying out the bass case as a box on the opposite side with a front button grid spanning several columns.

Still placing bass buttons...

I'm also planning two shoulder straps in brown leather that loop from the bass case top down to the treble case, running along the back of the instrument.

Settling on brown leather with gold buckles for the strap, and adding a clasp around the bellows. Now I'm working out the bellows fold details—about 15 alternating plates across the width, sizing each plate's thickness, height, and depth to create a convincing accordion-style bellows.

For the bellows plates, I'm alternating big and small plates to form a square-wave pleat pattern, coloring the big ones dark red and the small ones a deeper maroon, then adding gold trim lines along the pleat corners for a decorative accent.

I'll add corner guard boxes at the four bellows corners in gold for a cheap metal-guard look, plus thin pearl frame plates at the bellows ends. I'm planning to build everything without joints since static geometry stays in model space fine, keeping the color palette under the 64-flat-color limit and using around five SVG textures (swirl panel, grille, emblem, front plate, pearl shimmer) for the paint effects.

Now I'm adding feet and trim: positioning the bass/treble cases flush to the ground with the bellows slightly raised, then writing a helper function to add gold trim bars along the vertical edges and rims of each case. I'm defining a reusable box-building helper that creates parts without bone attachment since there are no joints, then starting to define the custom pearl paint material.

Writing pearl shader function...

I also need to merge geometries using mergeGeometries from three/addons since all the boxes share attributes, and I'm designing SVG textures: a floral swirl panel for the side caps with gold borders and a lyre motif, plus a dark grille texture with gold trim and slit rows for the top face.

Now I'm placing a small treble clef accent, then working out a vertical gold "Venezia" script plaque for the front near the keys, and planning emblem medallions for the end caps on both treble and bass sides.

I'm figuring out plane orientations so the textures face outward correctly, then adding five small pearl register-switch cylinders along the top front edge, positioned to avoid overlapping the grille.

Now I'm skipping the bass wrist strap and bass shoulder straps, adding a small gold bellows air-release valve cylinder on the back of the bass case top, and working out how to build a thin circumferential strap-and-buckle band around the bellows without obscuring the pleats underneath.

Still placing bellows components...

Adding a similar dark backing panel behind the treble keys for contrast. No feet needed, so I'm finalizing the layout and moving to write it out.

Working out the layered depths so keys visibly protrude from their backing: thin dark panel at the base, white keys stacked on top with proper depth, black keys raised further above those, with small gaps between white keys revealing the dark backing beneath. Now I'm starting to lay out the white key pitch and positions across the keyboard.

Placing black keys at the correct boundary positions between white keys following the standard piano pattern, then adding gold trim bars at the corners and edges of the case for decoration...

Actually I'm now shifting to the pearl-colored body box and a strap piece modeled as a sweep along a curved path, painted brown, running over the shoulder to connect the treble and bass cases.
